t: Number of Distinct Roll Sequences — DP over Last Two Rolls
o: Constraints couple three consecutive rolls: adjacent rolls must be coprime, and equal values must be more than 2 apart, meaning roll i cannot equal roll i-1 or roll i-2. So the state is the pair (previous value a, value before it b): transitions choose c coprime with a, c != a, c != b. There are only 36 states, and n up to 1e4 makes an O(n * 6 * 6) DP trivial. Precompute the 6x6 coprimality table once. Example n=2: pairs with gcd 1 number 22.
k: State = (last value, second-to-last value); only 36 states regardless of n.
Transitions require gcd(prev, cur) == 1 and cur different from the previous two values.

a.n: Approach 1: Rolling DP over Value Pairs
a.i: dp[a][b] = number of valid sequences of current length ending with ...b, a. For each next roll c, add dp[a][b] to ndp[c][a] when gcd(a,c)==1 and c != a and c != b. Initialize with all 6 single rolls.
s: Initialize dp[a][b] = 1 for all a,b (representing length-1 prefixes folded into the pair state).
Iterate n-1 times applying the transition; sum all dp entries mod 1e9+7.
a.t: O(n * 216) — 36 states times 6 transitions per step.

a.i: The transition is a linear map on the 36-dimensional state vector, so the whole recurrence is M^(n-1) applied to the initial vector. Fast exponentiation computes it in O(36^3 log n), useful if n reached 1e18.
s: Build the 36x36 transition matrix from the pair-state rules.
Raise it to the (n-1)-th power by repeated squaring modulo 1e9+7.
Multiply by the initial all-ones vector and sum entries.
a.t: O(36^3 log n) — matrix multiplications dominate.

w: The pair-state DP is the canonical solution — recognize that constraints look back exactly two rolls. Pitfall: the 'gap of 2' condition means equality with the immediately preceding OR second-preceding roll is banned, but a value may repeat at distance 3+. Follow-up: generalize to an s-sided die or gap of k, where the state grows to k-tuples.
